text:
Logan Wright: Dropping ADR draft for v2 cache telemetry cardinality budget + tags. Would love eyes from Platform + SRE on long-term maintainability + "oops we exploded tags" failure modes. https://confluence.redwood/…/adr-027-kv-cache-metric-cardinality-budget (WIP)

Allison Grant: Thanks Logan. Skimmed quickly. Overall direction is good. Main question: are we explicitly stating which dimensions are REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL vs "only in events"? Right now reads like we might allow tenant/route/model/region on everything.

Logan Wright: Good call. Intention is: counters/gauges -> required tag set only; structured events -> larger set (but sampled + post-processed). I can make that super explicit.

Priya Natarajan: +1. Also want clarity on what the platform will enforce vs what we "ask nicely". If enforcement is in pipeline, we need versioning + a safe fallback (aggregate/drop) when somebody ships a new tag.

Ethan Park: From control plane side: we can reliably attach `tenant_id`, `deployment_mode`, `region`, `route_id`, `model_id`, `model_version` at the gateway for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private, `route_id` isn’t always present (some customers bypass certain routing layers). ADR should call out the compat behavior.

Logan Wright: Yep. Draft has a short section but might be too hand-wavy. What do you want as the rule? `route_id=unknown`? or omit?

Ethan Park: Prefer `route_id=unknown` (single bucket) for metrics so dashboards don’t silently drop Private traffic. For events, we can include `route_hint` if present but keep it out of metrics tagset.

Sean Gallagher: Reading through the regression alerting angle: please don’t ship something that makes oncall chase their tail because cardinality got throttled and now hit-rate "drops". If we’re dropping series, we need an explicit metric like `cache.telemetry.dropped_series` or something so we can tell the difference between true regression vs ingestion guardrails.

Rafael Mendes: +1. And in the runbook we should include "check dropped_series + sampling config" before looking at runtime behavior.

Logan Wright: Makes sense. We already have generic pipeline drop counters but they’re not scoped to cache telemetry. I’ll add a section: mandatory guardrail metrics + dashboard panel.

Nadia Rahman: From pipeline implementation POV: I’m worried about a future where teams add `prompt_hash` or `request_id` “temporarily” and it sticks. ADR should explicitly forbid high-cardinality identifiers in metric tags (and list examples). I see it implied but not hard-lined.

Allison Grant: Agree. Use normative language: MUST NOT include request_id, trace_id, user_id, raw prompt prefix, etc. Provide the sanctioned alternative: hashed prefix bucket but only in sampled events, not in metrics.

Thomas Baird: On that: even “hashed prefix bucket” can blow up if we don’t cap buckets. If you do anything like `prefix_bucket=hash(prefix)%N`, pick N and document it. Also choose whether the bucket is computed at runtime vs pipeline.

Omar El-Sayed: Runtime can compute `prefix_bucket` cheaply, but only if N is fixed and we don’t do anything fancy (no string ops on hot path). We were planning to emit it only in the structured payload under a sampling flag.

Logan Wright: What N would you be comfortable with? Draft suggested 1k but not married.

Thomas Baird: 1k is fine for events if sampled. For metrics: N should be effectively 1 (don’t include it). And ADR should say the bucket is *debug-only*, not for primary dashboards.

Mei Lin: For backfill + long-term analytics: if we keep changing tag names/dimensions, we’ll suffer. Can ADR include a stable “attribution key” set and a deprecation policy? Like: we don’t rename `model_version` without a 1-quarter dual-write.

Priya Natarajan: +100. Maintainability is mostly about not breaking dashboards every 6 weeks.

Logan Wright: Ok: adding a section "Tag stability / change policy":
- metrics tagset changes require ADR update + 2-week dual emit (v1 + v2) if feasible
- dashboards use a canonical view layer, not raw metric names
- deprecations announced in #eng-platform and release notes

Cole Summers: Billing hooks note: we should be careful with “saved_prefill_ms” and anything that could get interpreted as billable savings. Please state these are observability-only estimates, not a billing source of truth, and ensure tags won’t let someone compute per-customer $$ without the billing pipeline.

Nadia Rahman: +1. Also for aggregation: if we include `tenant_id` + `route_id` + `model_version` + `region` on every metric, timeseries count could still get big. ADR should include an explicit budget number and what happens past it.

Logan Wright: Draft currently has: max 200k active series per region for cache telemetry metrics, hard cap enforced in pipeline with (1) drop least-used series after 15m, (2) always keep global aggregates, (3) emit `dropped_series` counter.

Sean Gallagher: If you’re dropping least-used, you can accidentally drop the “bad” route that only gets a small amount of traffic but is regressing. Prefer a deterministic collapse policy: replace `route_id` with `route_id=other` when exceeding budget, not random-ish dropping.

Rafael Mendes: Yes. “Other bucket” is way easier to explain in incident review.

Thomas Baird: Technically easier too. We can do top-K routes per tenant/region and collapse the rest. But be careful: top-K per tenant is still heavy. Maybe top-K globally per region and then `other`.

Ethan Park: From gateway: we can also pre-hash route IDs into a smaller set but I’d rather not. It makes troubleshooting miserable.

Allison Grant: Suggestion: ADR states a two-stage collapse:
1) Always keep global + per-deployment_mode + per-region
2) Keep per-tenant aggregates (no route/model) for everyone
3) Keep per-tenant+route for top routes only (configurable K)
4) Everything else collapses to `route_id=other` (single bucket)

Logan Wright: That’s good. I’ll rewrite the enforcement section to align with that rather than “drop least-used”.

Mei Lin: Please ensure whatever collapse happens is reflected in data model so analysts don’t treat `other` as a literal route.

Logan Wright: Will add: `route_id=other` reserved value; dashboards label "Other (collapsed)".

Mina Haddad: Routing concern: model routing fragmentation is one of the recs we want. If we collapse too aggressively, we’ll lose the signal (same tenant spreading across many model_versions). Could we keep model_version but collapse route? Or vice versa?

Sean Gallagher: From SRE perspective, route is usually the first place we look. Model_version is helpful but less actionable in incidents.

Priya Natarajan: For long-term maintainability, pick one primary axis for drilldown and make the rest “nice to have”. Otherwise we’ll keep expanding.

Logan Wright: Proposed compromise for metrics:
- Required tags on all cache metrics: `deployment_mode`, `region`, `tenant_tier` (hosted/free/paid/enterprise), `cache_policy_id` (small set), `model_id`
- Optional tags only on a subset of metrics (hit_rate views): `tenant_id`, `route_id`
- `model_version` only in events (sampled) + derived rollups in datasets (daily)
Thoughts?

Ethan Park: `tenant_tier` is good. `tenant_id` on metrics is ok if we enforce rollups. For Private, tenant_id is a local concept but should map.

Nadia Rahman: If `model_version` is only in events, dashboard drilldowns by version won’t be real-time. Is that acceptable?

Mei Lin: For Optimize recommendations, daily rollups are fine for MVP. Real-time per-version is going to be expensive anyway.

Mina Haddad: Works for me as long as event schema includes `model_version` consistently.

Allison Grant: ADR should explicitly say: version-level analysis is via sampled events / analytics dataset, not primary metrics.

Omar El-Sayed: Runtime can attach model_version to events easily (it already knows the loaded artifact id). For gateway metrics tags, keeping version out reduces churn.

Sean Gallagher: As long as oncall dashboards remain stable + we can trust hit-rate doesn’t “change” due to cardinality collapse, I’m happy.

Rafael Mendes: Can we add a hard requirement: any cardinality enforcement change requires SRE sign-off + dry run in one region?

Priya Natarajan: +1, and feature-flag it.

Logan Wright: Noted. I’ll add:
- enforcement policy is gated behind `cache_telemetry_v2_enforce_cardinality`
- staged rollout (dev -> canary region -> all)
- SRE sign-off checklist

Cole Summers: Also: mention we will not pipe any of these metrics directly into billing computations. (We keep getting asked.)

Logan Wright: Will do.

Allison Grant: Last nit: define “hit-rate” precisely. Some teams mean request-hit vs token-hit vs bytes-hit. ADR references multiple. Please align with spec doc (hit_bytes, saved_prefill_ms, etc.) and make sure ADR doesn’t redefine them.

Logan Wright: Yep. ADR will point to kv-cache-telemetry-v2-metric-spec for definitions; ADR focuses on tagset + enforcement.

Thomas Baird: :thumbsup: if you add fixed bucket sizes + forbidden tag list.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: with the “other” collapse + dropped_series metric.

Priya Natarajan: :thumbsup: once Private compatibility behavior is explicit.

Logan Wright: Great, thanks all. I’ll push an updated draft today and re-request approval in thread. Action items:
- [Logan] rewrite enforcement as collapse->other, add guardrail metrics
- [Logan/Ethan] document Private route_id unknown behavior
- [Logan/Allison] add explicit forbidden tags section + stability policy
- [Logan/Sean/Rafael] add SRE sign-off + rollout gate language
